source: Held-out IFHAS follow-up notes; hand-authored, frozen in git before any reader was run; synthetic

reports.text: Primary care review following the periodic adult screening. Blood pressure on two clinic readings today was 152/96 and 150/94 mmHg, and her home diary averages 148/92. Essential hypertension is confirmed. Ramipril 2.5 mg started and she will be reviewed in a month.

Seen in the cardiometabolic clinic. 24-hour ambulatory monitoring gave a mean of 144/91 consistent with sustained hypertension. Referred to the hypertension clinic; DASH diet leaflet and a salt-reduction plan given.
Follow-up for the raised pressure noted at screening. Today 124/78 on the repeat, and ambulatory average 121/76. White coat effect only. No hypertension; continue routine screening.
Her screening blood pressure was high (158/98). Today it is 150/95. We have asked her to record home readings for seven days and return with the diary before deciding on treatment.
Clinic BP 168/102 today, and 170/100 on repeat after resting. Stage 2 hypertension confirmed. Started on amlodipine 5 mg and lifestyle counselling today.
Review of an elevated screening blood pressure. Repeat measurements 118/74 and 120/76. There is no evidence of hypertension and no treatment is needed. Advised routine rescreening.

Her father has hypertension and was started on tablets last year, which worried her. For her own raised BP, a repeat reading today is still 146/92; confirmation requires ambulatory monitoring, which has been requested but not yet done.
Last year her BP was normal (122/80). Now two readings on this visit are 156/98 and 154/96 and hypertension is confirmed. Commenced on losartan 50 mg and referred to the dietitian for salt reduction.

Diabetes clinic intake after the screening HbA1c of 7.4%. A repeat fasting glucose today is 8.1 mmol/L, which confirms type 2 diabetes. Metformin 500 mg twice daily started and enrolled in the structured diabetes education programme.
HbA1c repeated: 6.9% (52 mmol/mol), diagnosis of type 2 diabetes confirmed on two results. Plan: lifestyle programme, dietitian review and metformin.
Repeat fasting glucose is 5.2 mmol/L and HbA1c 5.4%, so the raised screening glucose was a non-fasting artefact. No diabetes. Routine screening interval.
Screening HbA1c was 6.6%. A confirmatory fasting glucose has been ordered today; the result is not yet back. No treatment started.
HbA1c 6.1% at screening and today 6.2%: prediabetes range. We discussed risk, but she was asked to attend again in three months with a repeat HbA1c before any plan is made.
Prediabetes confirmed (HbA1c 6.0% twice). Referred to the diabetes prevention programme and given dietary advice; will be reviewed in six months.
Repeat HbA1c 5.6%. She does not have diabetes and does not have prediabetes. Return to routine three-yearly screening.
Confirmed random glucose of 13.2 mmol/L but she declined to start any medication or join the education programme today and wishes to think about it. Diabetes is likely; no plan agreed.
Her sister was diagnosed with diabetes in 2021. For this patient: HbA1c 7.8% repeated, diabetes confirmed. Started metformin, dietitian booked.

Lipid review after screening. Fasting LDL cholesterol repeated at 4.6 mmol/L (178 mg/dL) with a strong family history. Dyslipidaemia confirmed; atorvastatin 20 mg prescribed along with dietary advice.
Fasting lipid profile repeated: LDL 2.4 mmol/L, triglycerides 1.3 mmol/L. The earlier abnormal result was non-fasting. No lipid disorder; routine screening.
Screening LDL was 4.1 mmol/L. Repeat fasting profile has been requested today; she will phone for the result. No treatment decision made.
Triglycerides 6.2 mmol/L confirmed on a fasting repeat (very high). Referred to lipid clinic and the dietitian; fibrate considered by the specialist.

She is already on atorvastatin from another clinic according to the patient, but there are no records. Current fasting LDL is 3.9 mmol/L; we are waiting for the pharmacy record and a repeat profile before changing anything.
Repeat fasting lipids within normal limits. No hyperlipidaemia. There is no indication for a statin.
BMI 34.2 kg/m2 today (class I obesity). Referred to the weight management clinic and dietitian; exercise programme started.
Weight 98 kg, BMI 36. Obesity confirmed. Enrolled in the supervised lifestyle programme; orlistat discussed and started.
Re-measured at the clinic. The previously recorded weight was a transcription error: BMI is actually 24.8 kg/m2. Normal weight. No intervention needed.
BMI 31.5. She says she has recently gained weight after stopping smoking. Agreed to re-weigh in six weeks before offering a programme.
Her husband is enrolled in the weight programme. The patient's BMI is 33 and she has agreed to join the same weight management group starting next week; dietitian appointment booked.
BMI 22.9. She is not overweight and does not need referral. Waist circumference within the normal range.

Cardiometabolic clinic. Hypertension confirmed (clinic 158/96 and home average 150/94) and amlodipine started. Diabetes also confirmed with a repeat HbA1c of 7.1%; metformin started and referred for diabetes education.
Follow-up of two abnormal screening results. Blood pressure repeat today 119/76, normal; no hypertension. HbA1c repeat 7.2%: diabetes confirmed, lifestyle programme and metformin started.
Her pressure was 148/94 today: ambulatory monitoring ordered, result awaited. Fasting LDL confirmed 4.8 mmol/L, started rosuvastatin 10 mg.
BMI 35 confirmed: referred to the weight clinic and the dietitian. For the raised glucose, a fasting repeat is to be arranged and has not yet been done.
Both abnormal results were not borne out. LDL repeat 2.6 mmol/L (normal). BMI recalculated at 24 after correcting height. No dyslipidaemia, not overweight. Routine screening.
BP 162/100 and 160/98 on two readings: hypertension confirmed, perindopril started. BMI 32; discussed weight, she would like to try on her own for three months first and will return.
Hypertension confirmed, enalapril started. Dyslipidaemia confirmed (LDL 4.5), atorvastatin 20 mg started. HbA1c 6.7% is borderline - fasting glucose test ordered, result not yet received.
She did not attend her follow-up appointment for the abnormal screening results today. A reminder SMS was sent and the clinic will try to telephone.
No-show for the cardiometabolic review. For completeness, her blood pressure at screening was 160/100 and her HbA1c 7.0%, but nothing has been assessed or started because she did not come.
DNA: patient failed to attend the dietitian and weight clinic booking. Letter sent.
Patient attended the family medicine clinic for a repeat prescription of her asthma inhaler. Chest clear. Reminded about annual influenza vaccination.
Referral letter acknowledged. The patient is on the waiting list for a first appointment. No clinical assessment was recorded today.
Telephone call from her daughter asking about the clinic opening hours and parking. The daughter has diabetes herself, but no information about the patient's own results was discussed.
FOLLOW-UP | Domain: blood pressure | Repeat: 154/96 | Confirmed hypertension: yes | Plan: ACE inhibitor started, review 4 weeks.
FOLLOW-UP | Domain: glycaemia | Repeat HbA1c: 5.5% | Confirmed: no | Plan: none, routine screening.
FOLLOW-UP | Domain: lipids | Repeat: ordered | Result: awaited | Plan: to be decided.
FOLLOW-UP | Domain: weight | BMI 37 | Plan: bariatric/weight clinic referral sent.
BP in clinic 142/90. Hypertension is probable but she is to complete a week of home monitoring; no tablets yet.
Confirmed hypertension on ambulatory monitoring. She prefers non-drug management so we agreed a supervised exercise and weight-loss programme with the practice nurse; referral sent today.
Confirmed type 2 diabetes. No tablets for now as HbA1c is only 6.6%; she is enrolled in the diabetes education programme and the dietitian will see her on Monday.
Repeat total cholesterol 5.1 mmol/L, LDL 2.9, within target for her risk level. The screening flag is not confirmed as a disorder. No treatment; rescreen in three years.
Both blood pressure and glucose are raised again. Neither has been confirmed yet: ambulatory BP monitoring and a fasting glucose are both requested. Results awaited.
Diabetes confirmed (HbA1c 7.3%), metformin and education started. Lipids repeated and normal, no dyslipidaemia, no statin.
